phase3_external_candidates.b3_verdict: REJECTED by the stated reason each

rows: YES - with a disclosed protocol defect
NO as OCV; secondary cross-check only

why: the only candidate that is real measured, raw, openly licensed, LiFePO4, temperature-controlled, branch-separable AND has enough SOC resolution to preregister a split holding out >= 2 knee, >= 2 plateau and >= 1 transition observation while still calibrating every region

it is the same cell model as B1/B2's BATT_001, measured by a different laboratory with a different instrument, so the B1/B2 comparison is like for like in chemistry and design and independent in lab and protocol
the discharge branch is the one battery.cell.rint_ocv claims (discharge only); the charge branch is kept separate and used for hysteresis only
selection.why_not_by_model_performance: no candidate was scored by any model; the ranking above uses only the Phase 2 criteria
selection.disclosed_defect_carried_into_every_clai: the rest duration after each interrupt, the step current and the sampled point of the rest are undocumented anywhere retrievable. The voltage is therefore an interrupt-relaxed pseudo-OCV of unknown relaxation completeness, and B3 never calls it equilibrium OCV. Phase 8 (PREREGISTRATION.json) must carry an explicit, preregistered allowance for incomplete relaxation, with a sensitivity ladder, fixed before any held-out score.
selection.what_this_defect_does_and_does_not_block: It does not block testing whether an existing SOC-dependent representation can reproduce the measured shape of this branch on held-out points: every observation shares the same protocol. It does block any claim about the cell's thermodynamic OCV at a precision finer than the relaxation allowance.
selection.alternative_verdict_considered: BATTERY B3 BLOCKED - REAL DATA INSUFFICIENT. Rejected because a dataset exists that meets every hard criterion except full protocol documentation, and that defect can be carried quantitatively rather than hidden or used as a reason to stop.
